query_text: where does the sound come from when you crack your knuckles

content.text:
The “crack” sound from knuckles comes mainly from **gas bubbles rapidly forming inside the joint fluid**.

Your knuckle joints contain **synovial fluid**, a slippery fluid that lubricates the joint. When you pull or bend the joint, the space inside the joint capsule suddenly increases, which lowers the pressure. That pressure drop causes dissolved gases—mostly carbon dioxide—to come out of the fluid and form a bubble/cavity. The sudden formation of that cavity produces the popping sound.

This process is called **cavitation**.

Afterward, it takes a little time for the gases to dissolve back into the fluid, which is why you usually can’t immediately crack the same knuckle again.

For most people, occasional knuckle cracking is **not considered harmful**, though if cracking is accompanied by pain, swelling, or reduced motion, it’s worth getting checked.
